name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Jonathan Jackson running with large fundraising edge
model.rationale: The baseline of D+23.7 rests on a solidly blue Chicago district, an incumbent with a big money advantage, and no evidence of a competitive race; prediction markets agree at 96% Democratic. I keep the forecast essentially at the baseline with slightly tighter uncertainty.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or unexpected outside spending could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jonathan Jackson, the Democratic incumbent in Illinois' 1st District, is running for reelection in a Chicago-area seat that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 18 points. He won his primary and enters the general election with a large fundraising edge over Republican Christian Maxwell, who has raised only about $63,000. No independent polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the forecast relies on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money.

Prediction markets give Jackson roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, consistent with the quantitative baseline of a 24-point Democratic margin. With no signs of a competitive race, this district is rated Safe Democratic.
